description: A field-neutral doctoral seminar in which students survey a research area, present and critique papers, find open problems, evaluate artefacts and benchmarks, practise peer review, and prepare for qualifying examinations and a dissertation proposal. Weekly work uses research scenarios, reproducibility notebooks and statistical checks on published results, with examples drawn from many computing fields.
modelledOn: Booth, Colomb and Williams, The Craft of Research
Association for Computing Machinery, Artifact Review and Badging policy and Code of Ethics
Phillips and Pugh, How to Get a PhD
Wohlin et al., Experimentation in Software Engineering
outcomes: Survey a research area and build a structured, annotated reading list that exposes its main lines and gaps.
Present and critique a recent paper, separating claims from evidence and naming hidden assumptions.
Identify, formulate and position an open research problem with a defensible claim to novelty.
Assess benchmarks and artefacts for validity and reproducibility, and reproduce a published result with statistical care.
Write a constructive peer review and respond professionally to reviews of your own work.
Plan qualifying examination preparation and write a dissertation proposal with a realistic work plan.

units.title: Surveying a research area
topics: Scoping an area: boundaries, taxonomies and neighbouring fields
Building a reading list from seminal, survey and recent papers
Bibliometrics: citation networks, venues and how to read a field at scale
Annotated bibliographies and concept maps
Writing a literature map or survey section
Keeping current: preprints, alerts and tracking a living literature

units.title: Presenting and critiquing papers
topics: Structure of a paper presentation for a journal club
Separating claims from evidence in a paper
Hidden assumptions and threats to validity in published work
Comparing competing approaches on common ground
Leading discussion and giving feedback
Reading across fields: borrowing methods from a neighbouring discipline

units.title: Open problems and research gaps
topics: Telling gaps, open problems and fashionable problems apart
Mining limitations and future-work sections for problems
Negative results and failed replications
Formulating a problem and assessing novelty
Positioning a contribution: incremental, new method or new framing
Locally grounded research agendas and relevance to African needs

units.title: Benchmarks, artefacts and reproducibility
topics: Benchmark design, saturation, leakage and gaming
Evaluation metrics and statistical rigour: seeds, intervals and significance
Artefact evaluation: containers, documentation and badging
Reproducing a published result and diagnosing a discrepancy
Data, code and model licensing and sharing
Compute budgets, efficiency and low-resource research

units.title: Peer review practice
topics: Anatomy of a review: summary, strengths, weaknesses, questions and score
Judging soundness, novelty, significance and clarity
Confidentiality, bias, conflicts of interest and the use of AI tools in review
Writing rebuttals and responding to reviewers
Programme committee simulation and meta-review

units.title: Qualifying examination preparation
topics: Exam formats: written papers, oral exams, reading lists and research qualifiers
Breadth and depth: mapping the core areas of the field
Mock oral examination: thinking aloud and handling follow-up questions
Writing a critical survey or candidacy paper
Managing time, wellbeing and the supervisory relationship
Mentored teaching and communicating to non-specialists

units.title: Proposal and dissertation planning
topics: Thesis statement, research questions and contributions
Structure of a proposal: background, aims, methods and risks
Work plans, milestones, dependencies and contingency
Publication strategy: from papers to a compilation or monograph thesis
Funding, grant writing and research ethics approval
Choosing and working with a committee

units.title: Career, collaboration and impact
topics: Explaining your research in three minutes to a general audience
Authorship, collaboration and credit
Impact beyond papers: open source, policy and industry transfer
Proposal defence rehearsal

schedule.title: Scoping an area and building a reading list
schedule.exercise: Choose a research area, draw its taxonomy on one page, and assemble a reading list of 15 papers split among seminal, survey and recent work, with a line on why each is there.

tasks.title: Pick 12 papers from a given list of 30 for a reading list on a new topic in a scenario, and score coverage of seminal and recent work
Build a citation graph from a table of 80 papers, rank them by in-degree and betweenness, and identify the three most connecting papers
Cluster 200 abstracts by topic with a simple text model, label the clusters as a taxonomy, and judge where the area's boundaries blur

schedule.title: Annotating, mapping and writing the survey
schedule.exercise: Write annotations for ten papers, build a concept map linking them, and draft a one-page literature map that ends in a stated gap.

tasks.title: Turn 10 paper annotations stored in a table into a concept matrix of methods against datasets, and highlight the empty cells
Triage 20 new preprints in a scenario with limited weekly reading time, deciding which to read, skim or skip, and score the choices
Revise a draft survey section in a scenario that lists papers instead of synthesising them, grouping by theme, and score the argument that results

schedule.title: Presenting and dissecting a paper
schedule.exercise: Present one recent paper in ten minutes, then write a half-page list separating each claim from the evidence offered and the assumption each rests on.

tasks.title: Match 8 claims in a paper to the evidence supporting them in a scenario, and flag the claims that go beyond what the experiments show
Re-run an evaluation from a paper on a different data split and report which of its headline claims change
Recompute the statistics of a reported comparison from its summary table, check the stated significance, and find what the paper's test assumes

schedule.title: Comparing approaches and leading discussion
schedule.exercise: Compare two competing methods from the literature on the same problem under a common task description, and lead a fifteen-minute discussion with prepared questions.

tasks.title: Give feedback on a mock presentation in a scenario, balancing praise and critique, and score how useful and respectful the comments are
Compare two published methods on one shared dataset with the same metric and budget, and report where the original comparison was unfair
Adapt a method from a neighbouring field to your own problem in a scenario, justifying which assumptions transfer and which need testing

schedule.title: Finding gaps and open problems
schedule.exercise: Collect the limitations stated in eight recent papers, group them, and write three candidate open problems with the evidence that each is still open.

tasks.title: Extract future-work statements from 10 paper excerpts in a scenario and sort them into open problems, routine extensions and speculation
Attempt to replicate a published result and document the outcome as a short report, treating a failure as a finding rather than a mistake
Judge 6 proposed problems in a scenario as gap, open problem or passing fashion, using evidence on prior attempts, and justify each verdict

schedule.title: Formulating problems and positioning contributions
schedule.exercise: Write a half-page problem statement with a precise formulation, the closest prior work, and the specific way your contribution would differ.

tasks.title: Formulate a vague problem as an input, output and success criterion in a scenario, and score the precision of the statement
Position a contribution against five related papers in a scenario, stating what is new, what is borrowed and what is only incremental
Choose between a globally popular problem and a locally important one in a scenario with limited data, and defend the research agenda with evidence

schedule.title: Benchmarks and statistical rigour
schedule.exercise: Evaluate a benchmark for saturation and leakage, choose metrics with justifications, and write the evaluation protocol for fair comparison across seeds.

tasks.title: Plot the best reported score on a benchmark over 8 years from a given table, and judge whether it is saturating
Train a model with 20 seeds, report mean, spread and a confidence interval, and show that a single run can flip a ranking of two methods
Audit a shared artefact for missing files, hard-coded paths and unpinned versions, fix them, and run it clean in a fresh environment

schedule.title: Reproduction, sharing and efficiency
schedule.exercise: Reproduce one table of a published paper, explain any discrepancy, and write the licence and data statement you would attach to your own release.

tasks.title: Pick licences and write a data-sharing statement for a dataset with personal information in a scenario, and score legal and ethical fit
Reproduce a result from a paper's released code, track the difference to the reported number, and test three hypotheses for the gap
Reduce the compute needed for an experiment tenfold by subsampling and early stopping, and check the conclusion is unchanged across 10 seeds

schedule.title: Reviewing papers and responding to reviews
schedule.exercise: Write a full review of a short paper with a summary, strengths, weaknesses, questions and a score, then draft a rebuttal to a critical review of your own work.

tasks.title: Write a structured review of a draft paper in a scenario and score it for specificity, fairness and constructive suggestions
Respond to three reviews of your submission in a scenario, one unfair, answering with evidence and without defensiveness, and score the reply
Simulate a programme committee with 30 papers and noisy reviewers, compare acceptance by mean score and by discussion, and measure the agreement

schedule.title: Exam formats, breadth and the oral
schedule.exercise: Draft your qualifying plan: the exam format, the breadth areas you need to cover, a reading calendar, and ten likely oral questions with outlines of answers.

tasks.title: Plan the preparation for a written qualifying exam in a scenario with eight weeks, allocating time across topics and mock papers
Map the core areas of your field against your reading list in a table, compute coverage by area, and list the three weakest areas
Face a mock oral examination in a scenario with probing follow-up questions, thinking aloud and admitting gaps, and score reasoning and honesty

schedule.title: Candidacy paper, wellbeing and teaching
schedule.exercise: Outline a critical survey paper for your area with a thesis about the literature, and write a plan for a month with agreed meetings with your supervisor.

tasks.title: Handle a stalled research project and a tense supervision meeting in a scenario, choosing steps that restore progress, and score the outcome
Restructure a draft survey paper in a scenario so that it argues a thesis about the literature, and score argument and organisation
Explain a technical result to a mixed class and a policy audience in a scenario, adjusting depth, and score clarity and accuracy for each

schedule.title: Writing the dissertation proposal
schedule.exercise: Write a four-page dissertation proposal containing the thesis statement, research questions, method, a milestone chart, risks and a publication plan.

tasks.title: Refine a thesis statement through three critique rounds in a scenario, improving scope and testability, and score each version
Draw a Gantt chart for a three-year dissertation plan with dependencies, mark the critical path, and add a contingency for a failed experiment
Plan the publications of a thesis in a scenario, choosing venues, order and co-authors so that the papers form a coherent thesis, and defend the plan

schedule.title: Communicating, collaborating and the proposal defence
schedule.exercise: Deliver a three-minute public summary and a twenty-minute proposal defence rehearsal, and write down the five hardest questions you were asked with revised answers.

tasks.title: Rewrite a technical abstract as a three-minute talk for a general audience in a scenario, and score clarity without losing accuracy
Agree roles, authorship and data ownership for a collaboration across two institutions in a scenario, and score how well disputes are prevented
Defend a dissertation proposal before a mock committee in a scenario, answering challenges on novelty, feasibility and risk, and score the defence
